matchLines.fix: replace it with this repo's value (zip name, bump command, …) per the setup steps

failureMessage: the release config is explicit with no defaults — a missing/typo'd key would ship the wrong thing with no signal

whenMissing.what: missing — the release config is required and fully explicit (no defaults)
whenMissing.fix: create it with the required keys: {keys}

whenLineNotKeyValue.what: line is not KEY=value or a # comment: "{line}"
whenLineNotKeyValue.fix: use dotenv syntax — KEY=value, one per line

whenKeyMissing.fix: add "{key}=..." (every key is explicit; "setup_command=" may be empty to mean no install)

failureMessage: a version that diverges ships the wrong number to the store or refuses to publish

whenFileMissing.what: missing — the release pipeline builds via npm run build at the repo root
whenFileMissing.fix: add the root package.json with version equal to the manifest's

whenUnequal.fix: bump both together — "bump version" edits the manifest and package.json in the same change

failureMessage: the privacy page deploys from PRIVACY.md, and the store listing points at that live URL

requirePaths.fix: create it per the layout in the release standard (adapt from the reference repo)

failureMessage: every extension repo documents install and release the same way, from the standard template
fix: copy it from the README template in the release standard and fill in the repo values

whenMissing.fix: add a README with the standard Install and Releasing sections

failureMessage: the store requires a written justification per permission and blocks publishing the new version until the dashboard carries it; that step is manual, so a proactive issue beats the reactive publish failure

forbidAddedValueInArray.fix: open a tracking issue for the manual Chrome Web Store dashboard step: the Privacy-practices tab needs a written justification for "{value}" before the next publish can ship

failureMessage: the deployed privacy policy must disclose everything the extension can access; an undisclosed permission is a store-review and trust failure

requireIndexCoverage.what: manifest requests "{value}" but the privacy document does not mention it
requireIndexCoverage.fix: disclose what "{value}" accesses in PRIVACY.md, so the deployed privacy policy reflects what the extension can reach
